reviews.comment: Lectures are boring and sound monotone but short. What I hated that the homework HAD to be typed for physics?! Made me not want to do the homework because drawing physics problems and typing integration on a word document is not fun at all. I dont think other profs of this class forced u to type.

He is nice, but the lectures are very boring. If you pay attention he'll deliver useful info though. Attendance is mandatory for daily group quizzes over the material which are very easy. The final is very hard, but it's the same for every teacher. Lots of homework, but def manageable.

He's the best professor I know! Despite his monotone voice, he possesses a hilarious self-awareness and sense of humor. He puts so much into every lecture. I've gone into his office on multiple occasions and seen him doing the problems he assigns, researching related content, and reading books on how to be a better teacher of the subject.
Was a decent lecturer, would take again. Definitely very monotone but if you're actually showing up to lecture it's really easy to learn from him. He's also super responsive to questions.
He made quizzes and assignments in the class manageable and reasonable and even curved the final grades. I would take him again if I could, you should take him!!

I really enjoyed Professor McKenzie's class. His lectures are generally really good (although he can be a bit monotone), and he offers lots of opportunities for extra credit. Very accessible and I appreciated that he switched up lab groups every few weeks. Study well for the exams and take advantage of extra credit and you'll do well.
Very good professor. The lecture slides are pretty good. Exams might be a bit difficult, but he gives lots of extra credit.

He is a very, very nice guy. He is very helpful during class as well as outside of class. He gives extra credit opportunities, which helps your grade out a lot. Quizzes are really easy, and the slides are really helpful and go in-depth, which helps for the exams.
Boring lecture slides that are difficult to gain knowledge from. Final exam is a bear.

Professor McKenzie was overall an amazing professor due to his way of teaching the subject. He is one of the only professors who actually goes in depth into the code and shows you different codes from the lecture in the coding software. The extra credit is a life saver and got my grade to go up 7 points from just one of two extra credits.

Very sweet guy. Barely passed the class (due to my own shortcomings), but I still enjoyed it. He has a nice way of allowing us to meet new people, which involves us sitting with a new group he assigns every 3 or so labs. Met some great people because of this. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT! - which is completing all the participation and challenges in Zybooks

McKenzie really cares about his students, and he's a very chill and nice prof. I came into this class with no coding experience, but I was able to do well. Labs and quizzes are not graded harsh at all. The tests are the hardest part of the class, so do the extra credit he offers and make sure you understand the labs you're assigned every week!

He's chill lol. I like that he didn't require his students to do zybook modules unlike other profs. He's very open to giving extra credit and genuinely cares about his students. Only problem I guess I had is he talks kinda monotone, but that's about it.

He is a very nice guy, but the lectures were pretty boring as he pretty much just reads from the slides. He's very open to answering questions though, and has great explanations for the specifics. Exams are pretty difficult if you haven't coded before so definitely do the extra credit.

His lectures are helpful and in-depth if you don't have a programming background, and if you do, you'll have time to complete the mountain of zybooks homework he assigns (do it you'll get extra credit). It's a standardized course, so the sections aren't all that different, but his explanations of python concepts are pretty helpful.

Dr. Mckenzie is very nice but is kind of a terrible lecturer. To be fair, its not the most interesting course but his voice is incredibly monotone. He is very available to answer questions and it also actively trying to pass you with the crazy extra credit he gives. Exams are hard if you can't already code.

For a class as bothersome as ENGR 102, Professor McKenzie is the best that you can get. The class is mostly determined by two tests, but Professor McKenzie was generous with extra credit and graded labs and quizzes graciously. He's always willing to answer questions and will provide as much feedback as you ask for.

As a first-time coder, Zybooks will be your best friend. Quizzes are fine as long as you review the lectures beforehand. The only daunting part of this course was the final, which I feel is you either know it or you don't. Very nice professor and would make a great voice narrator if he ever pursued a side hustle.

He made us type out the homework, which was a pain and took a lot longer than necessary. He gave a good curve at the end, which boosted my grade to a B. He is very understanding. Lectures are boring, but I think that's the case for all 216 classes.

Nice person, abysmal prof. Monotone and slide-read lectures.The homework assigned was thankfully only once per week, but that weekly homework was nothing short of tedious and annoying. Most importantly, he does absolutely NOTHING to help prepare you for the final, all study materials provided are simple and shallow problems which pale to the final.

He is really kind and makes the class doable without much stress. The only stressful thing was the group project over the course of the semester. This was probably the easiest tech elective I've taken.

Only reason to go to class is the attendance assignment. His voice is pleasant to listen to and lectures are fine. Exam is not much tougher than the work you do throughout the semester. Other than labs, which are handled by PTs, requirements for each assignment are clear. Quizzes often allow you to analyze a problem before beginning the timer.

Super chill prof. The lectures can be monotonous, but he's super kind and is more than happy to help during office hours. He's also really understanding; if you miss a day or don't like your grade on an assignment, he'll still give you credit. Midterm is only 5% while the final is 25% of your grade, but that's the way 216 is in general.
Took him for 440 and 434. He is super nice and grades very leniently. Lectures can be pretty monotone. 100% recommend taking him if you get the chance.

Dr. McKenzie is a nice dude and a pretty okay professor. He can be a bit monotone though so bring caffeine or whatever else helps you focus to lectures. Occasionally there will be a quiz which he posts an announcement for the day before, and homework wasn't too hard with ample time to complete it. Second half of the course is a group project.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The course was easy with Professor McKenzie. Attendance was not mandatory and grading was easy. Only one test and one group project for the whole semester, which were not difficult

Professor Mckenzie is great, I took him for 216 and 102. He doesn't really care if anyone pays attention to his lecture or even goes, and he helps a lot if you ask him. You can pretty easily get an A if you put effort into the labs and the final. Fun fact: he used to play football as a backup for Mississippi state.

so much extra credit its insane. if u prelearn some python this class will be very easy. his voice is very monotone during lecture though so when i try to pay attention i struggle to stay awake. the extra credit takes a lot of hours to do, but you get half the semester for each opportunity and its so worth, boosted my grade like 9 points.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor McKenzie is a great professor and a great person overall. His lectures can tend to be boring but they are not horrible. Labs tend to be difficult and tests are hard. The extra credit adds a good 6-7 points on to grades so do them!

Dr. Mckenzie has a very monotone voice, and that, combined with an 8 am class, led to many students falling asleep. If you talk to him, though, he is exceptionally nice, and you can tell that he cares.

Dr. McKenzie uses example code during lectures, which helps when learning new concepts, especially for those who have never coded or are new to Python. He was very understanding when I asked questions about assignments, and he was clear about deadlines and expectations. However, some grades did take time to be returned. Very generous extra credit!

Having a good group really helps make the course easier. One thing I recommend is learning ahead using the Zybook textbooks, the slides usually do not offer enough information to help complete labs and will need to end up going through textbooks. Offers multiple extra credit, and quizzes are fair game if you do the homework in advance.

I came into this class with zero coding experience and found a way to get an A. At times he is very monotone and much of the learning you do will be from the labs. He offers extra credit, which helps your grade so much, got C's on both tests and still got an A because of extra credit and easy grade distributions. With coding experience its a easy A

Great guy. He is very caring and considerate and is very lenient on grading. On the weekly pop quizzes, he also gives tips and advice that are typically answers to the quiz that is about to occur. He makes the class much easier than others but has one crucial flaw. He is super boring and monotone. His lectures become nap time.

Dr. Mckenzie is a good professor and very caring. I am unsure if other professors did this, but he provided many example scripts during lectures instead of just reading from the slides. During the time for the team labs, he was accommodating and amazing at individual assistance. His voice is monotone and can lead to sleepiness, but he is fantastic.
Dr. McKenzie is a fantastic professor. Though his voice is very monotone and can lead to sleepiness, he is amazing at one-on-one help and is an overall amazing professor.

Like the other reviews said, his main drawback is his absolutely monotone and boring lectures. I had him early in the morning and half of the class was either asleep or on their phones. That being said, he is a passionate and good professor who I did genuinely enjoy and would probably take again. Tests are hard so study study study.
He gives decent feedback but his lectures were very boring, almost fell asleep every class.

Great prof who always would answer questions and be helpful whether inside of the room or through email. His homework was very long, but there's only one per week, and once you get the hang of it, it's not that bad. Overall, this class is difficult but he is a nice guy who wants to see you do good!

PHYS 216 is just generally a hard class, his lectures were recorded but not very helpful. His curve to the final was 4 points, which was just one less point for me to get an A. However, he was a nice prof and was clear with his grading.
No reason to go to THIS guys class, bro reads directly off of the slides. You're going to struggle in this course no matter what, but this guy will make you bored on top of that.

although Mckenzie's lectures can be monotone and at times hard to understand, he puts in a great amount of effort to help his students achieve a great grade, there are several opportunities for extra credit with generous curves. He is very kind and i would definitely take him again!!!

He has the most monotone voice on the planet but he is a sweet and passionate guy. The extra credit added more than 8% to my grade so DO IT. There is a quiz every week, and the exams are weighted heavily but they are doable, you wont pass them but that is normal. You will have a new group every week, which is annoying.

His class is not that hard, but he's very boring. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT!!. It's a free 100 quiz and lab grade, but it's not out of 100, it's out of 0, so it ends up adding like 6% to your grade and you can do it twice. He is not very helpful in class and even has to pull out his own computer to solve relatively simple things a professor should know.

A good prof who cares abt his students. Lectures can be boring, but its the material & not his fault. He's very accommodating if you're sick/need an extension, & gives out a lot of extra credit opportunity. If you need help on labs go to the TAs on the 4th floor. If you complete your labs & turn them in on time, you'll do good in the class.

TAKE A CODING CLASS PRIOR. I am going to receive an A in this class but if I had taken a coding class prior my grade would have been higher and the class would've required a lot less work. There is tons of coding hw every week. McKenzie is very very nice but his voice is very monotone and can make you fall asleep quickly. STUDY FOR THE TESTS.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. McKenzie was not a horrible teacher. He is a nice person, but his lectures are boring and hard to sit through. It is kind of obvious that he is not very good at coding either. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT, it helped a lot. I would not want to take him again.

Professor McKenzie was really easy to get in contact with and was lenient with extra credit and extensions. DEFINITELY do ALL extra credit offered so you have extra cushion for exam grades. ENGR102 is difficult by nature, especially if you have never coded before, but Professor McKenzie does his best to help. He can be a little monotonous.

I had him for ENGR 102, which is a freshman engineering coding class. His lectures were really boring, and I had a hard time paying attention and staying engaged. IDK how he is for 216, but for 102 I had to do a lot of googling for things not taught in class, and I was still confused. But the few times I asked for help, he gave helpful feedback.

His lectures are incredibly boring, his slides are unhelpful, and when he makes notes on them, they're impossible to read. The homework problems are lengthy and complicated, and the notes are only somewhat relevant. I had an extremely hard time in this class and the only reason I did good was because I had an amazing PHYS 206 professor.

Dr. McKenzie was a nice guy but it was very hard to pay attention in his lectures because of his monotone voice. The lecture slides were not very helpful, especially compared to the homework, and he did not explain the content well when asked a question/for help.

Dr. McKenzie is a great guy, and has pretty good slides and records all his lectures if you don't feel like coming in. The class is difficult by its nature, but the homework did a good job of preparing me for the final and labs- its the same as Dr. Ritchey's. Some other classes have better perks, like homework answer key quizzes.

This professor will make you fall asleep. He is very monotone, and his lectures are extremely boring. Attendance is not necessary; he posts his lectures on zoom. Compared to the other 216 classes, we had more homework and McKenzie's lectures didn't prepare you for the difficultly level of the homework.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He made this class unnecessarily difficult and aggravating in my opinion. He has a dull voice so it was rare for me to see a single person able to pay attention, the homework was confusing and lacked feedback, and he didn't respond to any emails in time. Unfortunately he is the worst prof I have had, and I am extremely nervous for the final.
Dr. McKenzie is great and very helpful outside of class. He does assign a little more homework than other PHYS 216 sections though. Overall he is very nice and is a good option for ENGR/PHYS 216.
